question.worked_solution:
First, note that $x=0$ and $x=\frac{1}{3}$ cannot be solutions since division by $0$ is undefined.

To solve the equation, we first apply cross-multiplication:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{2x} & =\frac{4}{3x-1} \\ 3\cdot (3x-1) & =(2x)\cdot 4 \\ 9x-3 & =8x\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we apply the addition and multiplication principles, as usual:

$$
\begin{aligned}9x-3 & =8x \\ 9x-3-9x & =8x-9x \\ -3 & =-x \\ \frac{-3}{-1} & =\frac{-x}{-1} \\ 3 & =x\end{aligned}
$$

Since  $x=3$ is different from $x=0$ and $x=\frac{1}{3},$ we can accept it as a solution. Thus, the solution is  $x=3.$
